sections.html:
A house here can move fast when the asking price matches its condition. Owners have three basic paths: accept an all-cash bid, hire an agent and go to market, or sell the place untouched. The decision rests on your calendar, the state of the building and how much effort you want to spend before closing day. The city calls itself the City in the Park and describes itself as a first-ring suburb of Dallas, so plenty of Dallas-area shoppers are close by.

Over half the housing units are rented, which means your buyer might be an investor, a landlord or a family. Each type wants something different, and the quickest routes usually skip the repair list in return for a lower figure.

  • Cash buyer: short closing, no fix-up demands, few visits.
  • Agent listing: broader exposure, inspection requests, a slower calendar.
  • Tenant-occupied house: lease review and notice steps come before anything else.

Farmers Branch has an estimated 38,320 residents as of July 2025, up 7.7 percent from 2020. Owners live in only 42.4 percent of housing units, so renters outnumber them.

sections.h2: City permits that touch a sale
sections.html:
Code Enforcement handles several permits that can come up while you prepare a house. Call them before you start, because a missed permit can hold up closing.

  • Garage and estate sales: registration is required. The limit is two sales per year, up to three consecutive days each, spaced at least seven days apart.
  • On-demand storage containers: a permit comes first, and the fee varies by location.
  • Single-family rental: the rental license is obtained through the city's self-service site.
  • Short-term rental: $120 per year, plus a passed inspection.

Sellers often empty a house with an estate sale or a storage container before listing, which is why the first two matter most.

Renting the house out changes who needs notice and what a purchaser inherits. Under city rules, a short-term rental is a single-family home let for 30 days or less. To operate one you need an inspection and a permit, processed by an outside vendor called Host Compliance.

The application wants a driver's license copy, the inspection report showing a pass, a floor plan with room sizes and a signed Chapter 26 acknowledgement. Buildings with three or more units need a multi-family permit, which lapses every December 31 and costs $13 per dwelling unit. A violation brings a $150 inspection fee per unit or building.

Should the new owner want to keep renting, check with Code Enforcement on whether the permit carries over or has to be reissued. When a tenant lives there and the lease says nothing about it, the usual first step is a written notice to vacate of three days or more. Any eviction case goes to justice court.

Lenders on Texas mortgages generally skip the courtroom, so a missed-payment problem can turn into an auction faster than owners expect. Once the default letter lands, the borrower typically has 20 days to make up the arrears. The sale notice then has to be out three weeks or more before the auction date.

Auctions take place early in the month on a Tuesday, during the day. Notices go up at the courthouse and into the county clerk's records. If the house sells and the price falls short, the lender has two years to bring a deficiency suit. When there is money left over, junior liens are paid ahead of you.

A closing that beats the auction date lets you settle the debt yourself. Ask the lender for a payoff in writing, then ask each buyer whether they can close ahead of the posted date.

No property tax is collected by the state itself. Cities, counties, schools and other districts set their own rates, while the appraisal district assigns each parcel a value based on its condition on January 1. Homestead owners get a notice near April 1. A protest is generally due by mid-May, or 30 days after the notice if that lands later.

Statements show up in October and go delinquent once January 31 passes. Since the January 1 lien rides with the land, closing normally divides that year's tax between the two parties. Call the county tax office for your parcel's balance and the city for its rate.

The new deed is filed with the clerk of the county where the house stands. That clerk's fee schedule sets what recording costs.

An organized folder helps every kind of buyer. Begin with the recorded deed, your latest tax statement, the loan payoff letter and the survey. Add receipts for roof, HVAC, plumbing and electrical jobs, and any city permit records for additions.

If the house was rented, add the current lease, the rental license number if you hold one, the deposit amount and the rent roll. A buyer who plans to live there will want the tenant gone by closing, while a landlord will want the lease assigned. Write your preference into the contract.

  • Deed, survey and tax statement.
  • Payoff letter and lender contact.
  • Permit records and repair receipts.
  • Lease, deposit and rent history for a tenant-occupied home.

Hand copies to the escrow office early. A lien or a misspelled name is far easier to fix weeks out. Ask the city, too, what becomes of a rental license when the owner changes.

An investor purchase usually removes the steps that eat weeks: no lender appraisal, no buyer financing contingency and no repair negotiation after the inspection. For a landlord with a tenant in place, that can mean the lease is simply assigned. For a house with an old roof or a code question, it means the buyer prices the problem instead of asking you to cure it.

The tradeoff is the number. Ask each investor for a written net figure, then set it next to what a listing would leave after repairs, commission and the extra weeks of carrying costs.

sections.h2: What to say in your listing
sections.html:
Stick to facts a buyer can check: year built, roof age, the last HVAC service and typical utility bills. If you are unsure about code history at your address, the city's Community Services department can tell you.

Disclosure forms should be plain and easy to translate, since many buyers here speak another language at home. After you accept an offer, keep a copy of every signed form. On closing day, compare the settlement statement with the contract, and confirm that any rental or short-term rental account has been closed out.

faqs.q: Can a Farmers Branch house sell quickly?
faqs.a: Yes, when the price fits. Buyers have plenty of nearby sales to compare, and your house is priced on its own condition rather than the $364,600 median.

faqs.q: Is a certificate of occupancy part of a Farmers Branch sale?
faqs.a: Ask Code Enforcement. The city lists a certificate of occupancy as a commercial requirement, so call before listing to learn what applies to a residential change of ownership.

faqs.q: Can I hold an estate sale before selling my Farmers Branch home?
faqs.a: Yes, with registration. City code allows two garage-type sales a year, each up to three consecutive days, and estate sales fall under that rule.

faqs.q: What does a short-term rental permit cost in Farmers Branch?
faqs.a: It costs $120 per year and requires a passed inspection first. Applications run through a vendor called Host Compliance.

faqs.q: How long does a Texas foreclosure take after a notice is sent?
faqs.a: Borrowers get a 20-day window to catch up after the default letter, and the auction cannot come sooner than 21 days after the sale notice. The sale itself is held on a Tuesday early in the month.
